scope: Only the two registered SDK repositories; no commit, push, PR, publication, deployment, consumer pin edits, owner operation replay, Handrail database/queue changes or new tasks/goals.
implementation: Gateway adds a negotiated bounded history bundle to the existing authorized history endpoint: up to four explicit control/page/changes reads, or at most five with dependent latest/context reads. Each constituent uses existing scoped store authorization; failures withhold the envelope. Body and constituent byte/page limits remain enforced.

Flutter spends a bundle only once inside its owning refresh. Client/account, conversation, activation, operation intent, window observation, generation and revision fences retain existing parsers, complete related coverage and approval/context paging. Incoherent envelopes fall back to ordinary reads; admission/recovery/exact-turn controls remain fresh and separate.

Stream and window invalidations retain follow-up demand across in-flight reads and moved deadlines. Concurrent observers share only an in-flight exact-turn observation read; independent cancellation, authoritative Stop and revoked-access eviction are covered.

JS invalidations honor the configured polling cadence instead of a fixed 100ms wake. Concurrent shared-tree changes preserving the one-second public default/caller cadence were retained and verified. Fresh prepare cannot use a refresh skipped during read backoff.

No host cache or separate recovery mechanism. Bundling reduces HTTP dispatches, not necessarily constituent database reads; comparison.json records both. Existing Flutter one-use preparation/related-coverage safeguards remain in place.
